Container.Name: OpenThreadBorderRouter-HA
Container.Overview:
Stand-alone build of the Home Assistant OpenThread Border Router add-on by ownbee (https://github.com/ownbee/hass-otbr-docker). It keeps the Home Assistant team's OTBR patches, settings migration and optional automatic firmware flashing for Home Assistant Connect ZBT-1/SkyConnect, without needing Home Assistant OS. Use the OpenThread-Border-Router template from this repository instead if you prefer the plain upstream image. Run only one border router per radio.
**1. Radio firmware**
The USB stick must run OpenThread **RCP** firmware (multiprotocol is not supported). Flash it with https://toolbox.openhomefoundation.org/, or set Auto-Flash Firmware to 1 to let the container install the Home Assistant RCP firmware on a ZBT-1/SkyConnect. Baud rate and flow control must match the firmware (460800 with flow control for Home Assistant firmware).
**2. Unraid network settings**
Settings > Network Settings: Network protocol **IPv4 + IPv6**. The container needs **host** networking and privileged mode (upstream: do not change these). Set Backbone Interface to the interface that carries your LAN (br0, eth0 or bond0).
**3. Host kernel settings (required)**
Docker cannot set network sysctls for host-network containers, so set them on the Unraid host (replace br0 with your interface):
`sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1` `sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1` `sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.br0.accept_ra=2` `sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.br0.accept_ra_rt_info_max_plen=64`
Unraid resets these at reboot and when DHCP renews the interface, so put them in a User Scripts script that runs **At Startup of Array** and on a schedule such as `*/5 * * * *`. accept_ra=2 keeps Unraid's own IPv6 address while forwarding is on. The container log warns when IPv6 forwarding is off.
**4. Home Assistant**
Add the **OpenThread Border Router** integration with URL `http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8081`, then open the **Thread** integration, make this network preferred, and on Android use the Home Assistant app's Settings > Companion app > Troubleshooting > Sync Thread credentials. Then add Matter devices through the Matter integration.
**Security:** the REST API and web UI have no authentication. Keep them on your LAN, or set Web UI Interface to 127.0.0.1 to hide the web UI. Back up the Data folder: it holds your Thread network credentials.
Docs: https://github.com/ownbee/hass-otbr-docker#readme · Home Assistant: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/otbr/
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: thread otbr matter border router openthread home assistant skyconnect zbt-1 rcp ipv6
Container.Requires: A Thread USB radio with OpenThread RCP firmware Unraid IPv6 enabled and the host sysctls from the Overview applied
Container.Changes:
### 2026-11-22 - Removed --sysctl flags: Docker refuses network sysctls with host networking, so the container could not start. Host settings are documented in the Overview instead - Added OTBR_WEB (the web UI never started without it), web UI interface, network radio and Thread beta options - Fixed log level values, default web UI port 7586 (8099 clashes with other apps), links and icon URL
### 2025-12-15 - Initial release

Config.Name: Radio (USB device)
Config.Description: Host path of your RCP radio, followed by :/dev/ttyUSB0. Find it with ls -l /dev/serial/by-id/.

Config.Name: TUN Device
Config.Description: Required to create the wpan0 Thread interface.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Thread network credentials and settings (keep a backup).

Config.Name: Radio Path (container)
Config.Description: Radio path inside the container. Keep /dev/ttyUSB0 to match the device mapping above.

Config.Name: Baud Rate
Config.Description: Serial speed of the RCP firmware. Home Assistant ZBT-1/SkyConnect/ZBT-2 firmware: 460800.

Config.Name: Flow Control
Config.Description: 1 = hardware flow control (Home Assistant firmware). 0 for radios without it.

Config.Name: Backbone Interface
Config.Description: Host LAN interface Thread is routed to (br0, eth0, bond0 or a VLAN like br0.3).

Config.Name: Web UI
Config.Description: 1 starts the OTBR web UI. The image only starts it when this variable is set.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: OTBR web UI port. Avoid 80 (Unraid) and 8080. If you change it, update the WebUI link in Advanced View too.

Config.Name: Web UI Interface
Config.Description: Address the web UI listens on, e.g. 127.0.0.1 for local only. Empty = all addresses.

Config.Name: REST API Port
Config.Description: REST API used by the Home Assistant integration (http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8081).

Config.Name: NAT64
Config.Description: 1 lets Thread devices reach IPv4-only hosts (cloud services, NTP).

Config.Name: Firewall
Config.Description: 1 blocks unsolicited inbound traffic to Thread devices (recommended).

Config.Name: Auto-Flash Firmware
Config.Description: 1 installs or updates Home Assistant's OpenThread RCP firmware on ZBT-1/SkyConnect at start. Leave 0 for other radios.

Config.Name: Network Radio
Config.Description: Optional IP:port of a network-attached RCP (for example a serial-over-TCP adapter). Also set Radio Path to /tmp/ttyOTBR. Untested upstream.

Config.Name: Thread Beta
Config.Description: Set to 1 to run the beta OTBR build (Thread 1.4+). Empty = stable.
